chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Harun ibn Kharja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, supplication during prosperity brings forth needs during affliction.

key_terms.الدُّعَاءُ: du'a — supplication, the act of calling upon God in prayer and petition; a pillar of the spiritual life in Islam
key_terms.الرَّخَاءُ: rakhā' — prosperity, ease, comfort, a state of material and spiritual well-being
key_terms.الْبَلَاءُ: balā' — affliction, trial, tribulation; divine testing that befalls believers
key_terms.الْحَوَائِجُ: ḥawā'ij — needs, necessities, desires that one seeks God's help to fulfill

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the importance of supplication during good times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that making du'a during times of ease and prosperity is not merely optional piety but a spiritual investment that yields dividends when hardship strikes. The Arabic word yastakhriju (brings forth/extracts) implies that prior supplication creates a kind of spiritual capital that can be drawn upon in times of need. This teaching was addressed to a community that understood du'a as a living relationship with God, not merely a crisis response.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Haroun Bin Kharija, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The supplication during the prosperity are instrumental for what one needs in the time of afflictions’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’Il ibn Mehran from Mansur ibn Yunus from Harun ibn Kharijah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Prayer and pleading before Allah for help in one’s enjoying well-being brings about (causes to happen) what one needs in the fall of misfortune.’”
